worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of a linear differential equation of the form ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(x)$ is given by $y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p},$ where ${y}_{c}$ is the solution to the homogeneous equation and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, we address the particular solution ${y}_{p}.$ Since $f(x)$ is an odd function, its Fourier series consists only of sine terms. For a second-order equation with no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an odd function. This is represented by the term

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

Next, we find the homogeneous solution. The characteristic equation ${\lambda }^{2}+5=0$ gives roots $\lambda =\pm \sqrt{5}\text{i}.$ So, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}x).
$$

To find the unknown constants, we apply the initial conditions. Using $y(0)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(0) & =A\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+{y}_{p}(0) \\ 0 & =A(1)+0+0 \\ A & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Note that ${y}_{p}(0)=0$ because the particular solution is a sine series.

Next, we use the derivative condition ${y}^{′}(0)=4.$ First, we compute the derivative of the total solution (with $A=0$):

$$
{y}^{′}(x)∼B\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{5}x)+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{b}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

Applying ${y}^{′}(0)=4$ and noting that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=1,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =B\sqrt{5}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{b}_{n} \\ B\sqrt{5} & =4-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{b}_{n} \\ B & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{n{b}_{n}}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $B$ back into ${y}_{c}=B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}x),$ we find the missing part:

$$
y(x)∼\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{5}x)(\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}-{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{n{b}_{n}}{\sqrt{5}})+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx).
$$

First, we address the particular solution yp. Since f(x) is an odd function, its Fourier series consists only of sine terms. For a second-order equation with no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an odd function. This is represented by the term yp(x)=∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nx).

Next, we find the homogeneous solution. The characteristic equation λ2+5=0 gives roots λ=±5i. So, we have yc=Acos⁡(5x)+Bsin⁡(5x).

To find the unknown constants, we apply the initial conditions. Using y(0)=0: y(0)=Acos⁡(0)+Bsin⁡(0)+yp(0)0=A(1)+0+0A=0 Note that yp(0)=0 because the particular solution is a sine series.

Next, we use the derivative condition y′(0)=4. First, we compute the derivative of the total solution (with A=0): y′(x)∼B5cos⁡(5x)+∑n=1∞nbncos⁡(nx).

Applying y′(0)=4 and noting that cos⁡(0)=1, we have: 4=B5+∑n=1∞nbnB5=4−∑n=1∞nbnB=45−∑n=1∞nbn5

Substituting B back into yc=Bsin⁡(5x), we find the missing part: y(x)∼sin⁡(5x)(45−∑n=1∞nbn5)+∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nx).
